source.author: verg
source.text: Tum dea nube cava tenuem sine viribus umbram in faciem Aeneae, visu mirabile monstrum, Dardaniis ornat telis clipeumque iubasque divini assimulat capitis, dat inania verba, dat sine mente sonum gressusque effingit euntis, morte obita qualis fama est volitare figuras aut quae sopitos deludunt somnia sensus.
source.text_original: Tum dea nube cava tenuem sine viribus umbram / in faciem Aeneae, visu mirabile monstrum, / Dardaniis ornat telis clipeumque iubasque / divini assimulat capitis, dat inania verba, / dat sine mente sonum gressusque effingit euntis, / morte obita qualis fama est volitare figuras / aut quae sopitos deludunt somnia sensus.
source.text_english: Then the goddess, in a hollow cloud, to Aeneas’ face, a thin shade without strength, a wondrous marvel to behold, adorns it with Dardan weapons and makes it resemble the shield and the crests of the divine head; she gives empty words, gives a voice without thought, and shapes the strides of one walking, such as, when death has been suffered, the forms are said to flutter about, or such as dreams, deceiving the senses at rest.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Furiosas Apollinis vates legimus; et illud Virgilianum: Dat sine mente sonum.
reuse.text_original: Furiosas Apollinis vates legimus; et illud Virgilianum: Dat sine mente sonum.
reuse.text_english: We read of the frenzied seers of Apollo; and that line of Virgil: It gives forth sound without mind.
